svg.title: The town of a link is the mB halo of its two coarse endpoints. It contains its parent and lies in the radius-mB+1 ball about that parent, hence in the radius-(m+1)B ball when B > 0. It can therefore be covered at scale B with at most steady(m) = ballCost(m+1) tiles. The visited receipt is the union of the towns of every link in the itinerary, including both its initial and final links. If d + 2 ≤mB, each successor parent belongs to the previous town and to the remaining visited receipt. These two sets meet. The covering inequality for meeting supports and induction give coverNumberB(receipt) ≤(k + 1) steady(m). For its tenure bound, any point in the first town lies within mB+1; a point in the rest is within d+2 of its next parent plus the induction bound there. Thus, when d + 2 ≤mB + 1, every receipt point lies within (k+1)(mB+1) of the initial parent. These establish the two geometric inputs used in the address count.
